title: January 6 Investigations, Courts & Legal Record
methodology: Each J6-L record preserves procedural posture. Allegations, congressional findings, convictions, dismissals, appellate rulings, pardons and commutations are recorded as distinct legal events and are not treated as interchangeable.

records.title: House Select Committee investigation and final report
records.summary: The House Select Committee gathered testimony, documents and other materials, issued findings and recommendations, and published a final report and supporting archive.
records.limitation: Committee findings and referrals are legislative findings; they are not criminal convictions or judicial findings of guilt.

records.title: Charges, pleas, trials and case dispositions
records.summary: Federal January 6 prosecutions produced different procedural outcomes, including charges, guilty pleas, trial convictions, acquittals, dismissals, sentences and appeals.
records.limitation: A criminal charge is an allegation. Each defendant must be described by the actual disposition of that person's case.

records.title: Convictions and guilty pleas remain distinct from charging records
records.summary: Where a defendant pleaded guilty or was convicted at trial, that adjudicated result should be preserved separately from the original charging document and from any later appeal or clemency.
records.limitation: A conviction in one case does not establish guilt for another defendant, another charge, or a broader political claim.

records.title: Fischer v. United States narrowed 18 U.S.C. §1512(c)(2)
records.summary: The Supreme Court narrowed the circumstances in which the obstruction provision in 18 U.S.C. §1512(c)(2) may be applied, affecting a subset of January 6 cases.
records.limitation: Fischer did not erase every January 6 prosecution or invalidate unrelated charges, convictions or conduct.

records.title: Trump v. United States established an immunity framework
records.summary: The Supreme Court established a framework distinguishing exclusive constitutional authority, other official acts and unofficial acts when evaluating criminal prosecution of a former president.
records.limitation: The decision did not itself determine guilt or innocence on the federal election-related allegations.

records.title: Federal election-related prosecution ended without a trial verdict
records.summary: The federal election-related case against Donald Trump was dismissed before trial after the 2024 election under the Justice Department's position concerning prosecution of a sitting president.
records.limitation: A dismissal before trial under a presidential-prosecution policy is not a trial conviction and is not an acquittal on the factual merits.

records.title: January 2025 pardons and commutations changed legal consequences
records.summary: Presidential clemency covered federal January 6 offenses through pardons, commutations and directions concerning pending covered cases.
records.limitation: Clemency is a later executive action. It should not be presented as an appellate reversal of the historical charging, plea, verdict or sentencing record.

records.title: Preserve the complete legal sequence
records.summary: For significant proceedings, the record should preserve allegation or charge, adjudication, appeal, later court ruling, dismissal, clemency and current status as separate events.
records.limitation: Later developments should update the current status without silently overwriting what occurred earlier in the procedural history.
